name: Unidiso
tagline: Every solution a university needs, in one place.
meta_desc: Unidiso builds the digital backbone of universities: ERP, timetabling, academic performance, CRM, ticketing and efficiency analytics.

hero.title: Every solution a university needs, in one place.
hero.lead: From timetabling to academic performance, from resource planning to support requests — build your campus's digital backbone with products that talk to each other.
hero.note: Each product is sold separately; they work together.

products_head.title: One product for every part of campus
products_head.lead: Start with the module you need; add others as they become necessary. All products share the same data model.

products.name: SERP
products.short: Simplified enterprise resource planning shaped by the needs of a real university. Procurement, budget, meetings, events and reporting in one system that needs no technical background.
products.page_title: An ERP designed for universities, usable by everyone
products.lead: When general-purpose ERP systems are adapted to a university, the result is heavy, complex screens that staff avoid. SERP took the opposite route: it was shaped inside a real university's daily operation, one process at a time. Unnecessary detail was removed; from procurement to budget, meeting management to event planning, every process runs on simple screens that anyone from the rectorate to a department secretary can use from day one.

features.title: Procurement and supplier management
features.text: Requests, approvals, supplier records and order tracking end to end. Every step is recorded, every approval sits with the authorised role.

features.title: Budget management
features.text: Budget planning by unit and line item; spending matches budget lines and deviations are visible immediately.

features.title: Meeting management
features.text: Agenda, attendees, decisions and action items in one place. Decisions are assigned to an owner and followed until closed.

features.title: Event planning
features.text: Institutional events planned with venue, resource and calendar management, linked to budget.

features.title: Management dashboard and reporting
features.text: Summary indicators by faculty and unit at a glance. Any report, in any format, at any interval.

features.title: Open integration
features.text: Connects to the student information system, accounting, e-signature and every other external system the institution already uses.

detail.title: Fast to roll out, faster to adopt
detail.text: Most ERP projects fail not because of the software but because staff never move onto it. Because SERP's screens are simple, the entire staff switches over after a short training and processes run through the system from the first week. A high-performance infrastructure means no waiting even in peak periods.
bullets: A simple, role-based interface the whole staff adopts quickly
Scalable infrastructure that stays fast in peak periods
Reports produced instantly, exactly the way management wants them
Two-way, open integration with existing systems

screens: Module panel — every process on one screen

products.name: D-plan
products.short: Builds the term and annual timetable fully automatically. Room, lecturer and course data arrive once via integration; a month of planning shrinks to three days.
products.lead: Timetable preparation — weeks of work at the start of every term, running through spreadsheets and email threads — is one of the processes where universities lose the most time. D-plan makes it fully automatic within the rules the institution defines. Room, lecturer and course data are pulled once from institutional systems through integration; the planner enters no data and only reviews and publishes the result.

features.title: Fully automatic planning
features.text: The entire term or annual timetable is generated by the system within the defined constraints; per department or for the whole university in one run.

features.title: Integrated data, zero manual entry
features.text: Rooms, lecturers, courses and student groups come automatically from the student information system. Nothing is re-uploaded each term.

features.title: Rule-based constraints
features.text: Room capacity and equipment, lecturer availability, building/campus distance and the institution's own rules are part of the plan.

features.title: Clash-free result
features.text: Lecturer, room and student-group clashes are prevented while the plan is generated; no corrections afterwards.

features.title: Room availability and floor-plan view
features.text: Which room is busy on which day and hour, and which is free — as a list and on the building floor plan.

features.title: Publish to any system
features.text: The generated timetable is sent in one step, via open integration, to the student portal, lecturer portal, SIS and calendar apps.

detail.title: A month of planning, down to three days
detail.text: At the university using D-plan, term planning that previously took about a month dropped first to a week and then to three days. The timetable is live today in student and lecturer portals; lecturer availability and room data are pulled from the system automatically every term.
bullets: Planning time went from one month to three days
Data is pulled once via integration, never re-entered each term
Clashes are prevented during generation; nothing to fix afterwards
Output is delivered to any system, including student and lecturer portals

products.name: A-Score
products.short: Collects YÖK Akademik, Scopus and TR Dizin data automatically and turns each academic's real academic value into a measurable score using the institution's own criteria.
products.lead: An academic's value sits scattered across sources — publications in YÖK Akademik, citations in Scopus, national work in TR Dizin. Collecting it by hand takes weeks and sparks a dispute every time. A-Score gathers the data from these sources for every academic automatically, matches it and turns it into a single performance score using the institution's criteria. The data layer is extensible: Web of Science or Google Scholar can be added tomorrow.

features.title: Multi-source, automatic data
features.text: Articles, proceedings, books, thesis supervisions and citations are pulled from YÖK Akademik, Scopus and TR Dizin; cross-source matches (YÖK–Scopus, Scopus–TR Dizin) are detected.

features.title: Institution-specific performance score
features.text: Parameters such as publications, citations, seminars and teaching load are scored on target-versus-actual with the percentage weights the institution sets.

features.title: Flexible criteria management
features.text: Administrators add new criteria and set their weight; the calculation updates immediately. Each faculty can use its own criteria set.

features.title: Comparison
features.text: See two academics, departments or faculties side by side by publications, citations and year.

features.title: Faculty and university reports
features.text: Publication distribution, yearly trends and performance summaries at faculty/department and university level as ready reports.

features.title: Academic profile
features.text: Every academic can review their publications, yearly distribution and performance grade in their own profile.

detail.title: An indicator of real academic value
detail.text: Rectorate, deans and department heads see each academic's value based on data, not estimates; appointment, promotion and incentive decisions rest on a transparent calculation. Academics follow where their score comes from and which criteria they are missing in their own profile.
bullets: Publication and citation data is never collected by hand; it is pulled and matched automatically
Criteria and weights belong to the institution; the calculation is transparent and traceable
A shared panel for rectorate, deans and department heads; a personal profile for each academic
An architecture that accepts new data sources

products.name: CRM – Campaign Management
products.short: Brings prospect data from every source into one place and runs enrolment and preference periods in a planned way through SMS, email, social media, call-centre, IVR and AI Voice campaigns.
products.page_title: Run enrolment and preference periods from one place
products.lead: During preference and enrolment periods, prospective-student data flows separately from web forms, external application platforms, fairs and the call centre; who was called and who received a message is often unclear. CRM – Campaign Management merges these scattered sources into a single prospect pool. Undergraduate, graduate, lateral-transfer, vertical-transfer, international and special-talent applications are tracked separately; prospects are grouped and a campaign is planned for each group on the right channel, with its result followed on the same screen.

features.title: One prospect pool
features.text: Tens of thousands of prospect records from web forms, external application systems and outreach events in one pool; source and channel recorded on every entry.

features.title: Tracking by application type
features.text: Undergraduate, graduate, lateral transfer, vertical transfer, international, special talent, workshop and campus-visit applications in separate flows, one panel.

features.title: Segmentation
features.text: Prospects grouped by application type, programme interest, city and behaviour; a different message and channel for each group.

features.title: Multi-channel campaigns
features.text: SMS, email and social-media campaigns planned and sent from one calendar.

features.title: Voice outreach and AI Voice
features.text: Call-centre calls, IVR and AI-driven voice calls (AI Voice) managed within the same plan; every call is recorded.

features.title: Dashboard and conversion reports
features.text: Total prospects, application-type breakdown, monthly application trend and prospects by programme at a glance; how many applications each channel brought is measured.

detail.title: Every channel, one plan
detail.text: Messaging, calling and social campaigns are planned on the same prospect data rather than in separate tools. No prospect is called twice, none is forgotten, and the return on the outreach budget is visible as a number.
bullets: All prospect sources and application types in one system
SMS, email, social media, IVR, AI Voice and call centre from one plan
Measurable campaign management with monthly trends and channel-based conversion reports
Enrolled prospects are transferred to the student information system

screens: Dashboard — application type and source breakdown

products.name: Ticket Management
products.short: Student or staff, whichever channel they use, every request lands in one system; the right unit answers, every request is followed until closed, and none is lost.
products.lead: In a university, requests come from everywhere: a student writes through the portal, a lecturer sends an email, a parent phones, a staff member reaches out on WhatsApp. When each channel lands with a different person, requests are forgotten, the same problem is asked three times and nobody knows how many requests came in. Ticket Management collects requests about every process in the institution, from students and staff alike, in one queue; each request lands with the relevant unit, is assigned an owner and followed until closed.

features.title: Every channel into one queue
features.text: Portal, email, mobile app, WhatsApp and phone all feed the same system; however the user reaches you, the request lands in the same place.

features.title: Students and staff, internal and external
features.text: Students, lecturers, administrative staff and external stakeholders open requests from the same system; each sees the status of their own requests.

features.title: Unit-based handling
features.text: Requests are routed to the relevant unit by category; unit users answer and, if needed, hand over to another unit.

features.title: Every process in the institution
features.text: IT, student affairs, technical services, library, finance — whichever unit, the same flow.

features.title: Traceability and history
features.text: Who handled each request, when and what was answered is recorded; a user's past requests on one screen.

features.title: Reporting
features.text: Request volume, open/closed counts and resolution times by unit, category and period.

detail.title: Nobody's problem slips through
detail.text: Whatever channel a request arrives from, it is recorded, assigned to an owner and followed until it is closed. Management sees how many requests reach each unit and where they pile up; staffing and process decisions rest on data.
bullets: Portal, email, mobile, WhatsApp and phone in one queue
Every request has an owner, a status and a history
All units of the institution in one system, one flow
Request volume and resolution reports by unit

products.name: Academic Staff Efficiency
products.short: Proves academic staff's internal efficiency with ratios — courses taught, teaching capacity and coverage rates per course — and compares faculties and departments.
products.lead: This product is different from A-Score: it measures internal performance, not publications and citations. How many courses does a lecturer teach, how many could they teach, how much of each course was delivered, where do they stand in internal evaluations? Academic Staff Efficiency answers these questions with data pulled from the timetable and institutional sources — based on ratios, not estimates.

features.title: Teaching load and capacity
features.text: Courses taught compared with courses that could be taught; lecturers at full capacity and those with room are visible.

features.title: Course coverage
features.text: How much of each course's planned syllabus has been delivered, as a percentage; gaps are spotted before the term ends.

features.title: Internal evaluation criteria
features.text: The institution's evaluation criteria and weights enter the calculation; different criteria sets can be defined per faculty.

features.title: Faculty and department view
features.text: Overall evaluation summary, criteria distribution by faculty, highest- and lowest-performing lecturers.

features.title: Lecturer list
features.text: Each lecturer's teaching load, coverage rate and evaluation score in one sortable, filterable table.

features.title: Integrated and open data
features.text: Data pulled automatically from the timetable (D-plan) and the student information system; integration with any system.

detail.title: Proves performance with ratios
detail.text: Whose capacity is full, where there is room, which courses fall short on coverage — deans and department heads make course-distribution and staffing decisions with data. The evaluation conversation with a lecturer rests on numbers, not argument.
bullets: Automatic data from the timetable and institutional sources; no manual entry
Teaching load, capacity and coverage rate calculated in one place
Comparable, provable ratios by faculty and department
Used with A-Score, academic and internal performance sit on the same panel

screens: Evaluation summary — load ratio and composite score
Course coverage — lecturer and section distribution

products.name: Classroom Efficiency
products.short: Who is in which room, when it should open, how many students will come, how many desks there are — makes classroom use manageable and delivers measurable savings in space and energy.
products.lead: One of an institution's biggest and least visible problems is classroom use: which lecturer is in which room, when should the room open, how many students will come, how many desks and what equipment are there? When these questions go unanswered, classes run in large rooms with few students, empty rooms are heated, and the case for a new building is built on a problem that may not exist. Classroom Efficiency answers all of these on one screen, on the building floor plan.

features.title: Room–course–lecturer matching
features.text: Which lecturer, in which room, on which day and hour; automatic from D-plan timetable data.

features.title: Capacity fit
features.text: Expected student numbers compared with the room's desks and equipment; large rooms for small classes and small rooms for large classes are flagged.

features.title: Opening and usage hours
features.text: When each room opens, how long it is used and when it stands empty is clear.

features.title: Sensor support
features.text: Sensors in classrooms feed real usage data into the system; the gap between planned and actual use becomes visible.

features.title: Floor plan and availability map
features.text: Rooms on the building floor plan together with occupancy; the weekly availability table at a glance.

features.title: Building and campus summary
features.text: Classroom efficiency reported at building, faculty and campus level as a basis for investment decisions.

detail.title: Economic and spatial gains
detail.text: Once room details are manageable, idle space and unnecessary opening hours disappear. Heating, lighting and cleaning costs fall, and because existing space is used better, the need for new classrooms is judged on data.
bullets: Room, lecturer, student numbers and equipment on one screen
Planned-versus-actual usage with sensors
Measurable savings in space and energy cost
With D-plan: efficiency findings feed the next term's plan

screens: Rooms free right now — weekly availability
Floor plan: occupancy on the building plan
